hero.caption: Our letter's estimate of the money that leaks between a signed quote and a finished install, for every hundred cabs shipped
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: Built to be corrected, not believed.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Cabs you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per hundred cabs.

spans.text: Your posted starting prices, $8,147 to $12,724 by model and capacity [[OBSERVED]], fabacab.com/elevate, as of September 25, 2026. Constants in this model, not sliders.

sliders.label: Share of jobs rebuilt in whole or in part
sliders.basis: Your pricing page names wrong field dimensions as the one thing that reopens a final, out-the-door price [[OBSERVED]]. No one in your trade publishes a remake rate, so this range is assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Materials as a share of a cab's price
sliders.basis: The share of your posted price that is material rather than labor and margin. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Months between signature and shipment

presets.label: We buy materials the day we quote

sliders.basis: The window across which a fixed, all-inclusive quote absorbs material moves, from signature to purchase. Your site publishes eight to ten weeks after signed approvals [[OBSERVED]]; the band allows for the wait before approvals too. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

constants.text: Aluminum mill shapes rose 25.3 percent from September 2025 to August 2026 [[BENCHMARK]], BLS series WPU102501, 295.898 to 370.902. The model uses the published 25.3; the unrounded change is 25.3479 percent.

terms.label: Jobs rebuilt at your posted prices
Material drift absorbed inside fixed quotes

model.formulaText: Leak per 100 cabs = 100 × remake rate × posted price + 100 × posted price × materials share × 0.253 × (months / 12)
model.plainText: In words, the cabs that get rebuilt at your own posted prices, plus the slice of this year's aluminum rise that a fixed quote absorbs while it waits between signature and purchase.

market.heading: The market behind the number
market.intro: You sell into the one corner of construction still growing, while the metal a cab is made of costs 25.3 percent more than last September [[BENCHMARK]].

charts.title: Aluminum mill shapes, September 2025 to August 2026

charts.callout: Up 25.3 percent from September 2025 to August 2026. The unrounded change is 25.3479 percent.

charts.title: Published lead times
charts.unit: Weeks, as published by each company, September 2026
charts.callout: qCab publishes four weeks or less, SnapCab Express five to six weeks, and your site eight to ten weeks after signed approvals. Each bar is drawn at the top of its published range. If the gap is custom scope, it is a pricing asset.
charts.source: qCab, SnapCab and FabACab published pages, September 2026.

notes: Otis booked 26 percent more modernization orders worldwide last year [[BENCHMARK]], at constant currency.
US construction spending overall fell 3.8 percent in the year to July [[BENCHMARK]].

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Your About page credits the Cab Builder with changing the way elevator interiors are quoted [[OBSERVED]]. Your handrail carries a patent written so the installer never enters the hoistway [[OBSERVED]]. You post starting prices and cab weights on the open web; of seven competitors we read, none posts both [[OBSERVED]].
You build in Anderson, with satellite locations in New York, Chicago, Memphis and Las Vegas [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal is deliberately small. In two to three weeks, for a fixed fee between $1,500 and $2,500 settled in one call, we would measure four numbers from your records: the remake rate and its cost by cause, what your quotes absorbed, where time goes inside your lead time (qCab publishes four weeks or less, SnapCab five to six express, your site eight to ten after approvals), and the modernization share of your order book. Read-only; nothing installed, nothing changed.

deliverables.title: The remake rate, by cause
deliverables.line: Every rebuilt job in your records, counted and costed, split into field measurement, submittal misread, freight damage and shop error, with every classification confirmed by your people before it counts.

deliverables.title: What your quotes absorbed
deliverables.line: Each job's materials priced at quote date and again at purchase date against the public index, so you see the drift a fixed, all-inclusive price ate. If you buy the day you quote, this measurement returns zero and we say so in writing.

deliverables.title: Where time goes inside your lead time
deliverables.line: Your eight to ten weeks split into working time and waiting time as far as your records allow, set beside the published lead times above.

deliverables.title: The modernization share of your order book
deliverables.line: Your orders split between modernization and new construction, by quarter, set against the Otis and Census series.

ledger.title: What a page of the remake log looks like
ledger.label: Illustrative, not FabACab data

rows.flag: Rebuilt in whole for damage in transit. The one cause of the four that never touches your shop's workmanship.

ledger.note: Per job. Cost is the posted price times the share rebuilt. Causes are the four buckets the measurement uses. Every job and figure is invented to show the format.

proposal.weeksHeading: How the two to three weeks run

weeks.what: Your records arrive and we build the inventory: what exists and what is missing, per measurement. The data-readiness verdict comes in writing either way.
We build the four measurements, confirm every remake classification with your people, and deliver the baseline memo, the measured numbers and the corrected model. You review before anything is final.

proposal.fee: A fixed fee between $1,500 and $2,500, settled in one call.
proposal.feeCovers: It covers all four measurements, the first-week verdict, the readout and the hand-over. Read-only; nothing installed, nothing changed, and nothing billed by the hour.
proposal.conversion: If your records cannot support the four measurements, we say so in the first week and deliver a data-readiness report at the same fee.
proposal.promise: If your records show our letter overstated the money, the baseline says so in writing.
